title: Clausulas de participio y causativo (have/get something done)

lesson.intro: Dos recursos de nivel C1. El causativo (have / get + objeto + participio) dice que otra persona hace el trabajo por ti (o que algo te pasa). Las clausulas de participio (-ing, -ed, Having done) comprimen una oracion subordinada en una frase mas corta y formal.

sections.heading: 1 - Causativo: have something done
sections.body:
Estructura: have + objeto + participio pasado. Significa que otra persona (normalmente un profesional) hace el trabajo por ti.

El objeto va siempre entre have y el participio.
examples: I had my car repaired. (un mecanico lo hizo)
We're having the kitchen painted.
She had her photo taken for the passport.
Compara: I painted the house. (yo) / I had the house painted. (un pintor)

sections.heading: 2 - Causativo: get something done
sections.body:
get + objeto + participio pasado. Mismo significado que have something done pero mas informal y frecuente al hablar.

Ojo: get + persona + to + infinitivo = conseguir / persuadir a alguien de que haga algo; have + persona + infinitivo sin to.
examples: I need to get my hair cut.
Let's get the car washed.
I got the plumber to fix the leak.
I had the plumber fix the leak. (sin 'to')

sections.heading: 3 - have/get something done: experiencias
sections.body:
La misma estructura describe algo (a menudo malo) que te pasa sin que lo hayas provocado.

El contexto dice si es un servicio o una desgracia.
examples: I had my wallet stolen.
She had her house broken into while on holiday.
They had their flight cancelled.
He had his nose broken in the fight.

sections.heading: 4 - El causativo en distintos tiempos
sections.body:
Lo que cambia de tiempo es have / get; el participio no cambia.

  • Present continuous: I'm having it done.
  • Past simple: I had it done.
  • Present perfect: I've had it done.
  • Futuro: I'll have it done / I'm going to have it done.
  • Modales: You should have it checked.
  • Con -ing: I hate having my photo taken.
examples: We are having the bathroom retiled at the moment.
She has had her portrait painted.
I'll have the car checked before the trip.
By next week we'll have had the fence repaired.

sections.heading: 5 - Clausulas de participio con -ing
sections.body:
Sustituyen a una clausula con as / because / while / when + sujeto + verbo cuando el sujeto es el mismo que el de la principal. Tienen sentido activo.

Sirven para causa (Feeling tired, she left = Because she felt tired) o para dos acciones simultaneas (She left, slamming the door).

Cuidado con el dangling participle: el sujeto de ambas partes debe coincidir.
examples: Feeling tired, she went to bed.
Walking home, I met a friend.
Not knowing what to say, he stayed silent.
She left, slamming the door.

sections.heading: 6 - Clausulas de participio con -ed
sections.body:
Empiezan por un participio pasado y tienen sentido pasivo (una pasiva reducida): Built in 1850, the bridge... (= It was built...).

Sirven tambien para condicion (Cooked properly, this dish is delicious) o para describir un estado.

Formulas frecuentes: Given..., Faced with..., Compared with..., Based on..., Seen from...
examples: Built in 1900, the house needs work.
Given the choice, I'd stay.
Shocked by the news, she sat down.
The soldiers, exhausted, kept marching.

sections.heading: 7 - Having + participio
sections.body:
Having + participio indica una accion terminada ANTES de la accion principal (= After he had...).

Pasiva: Having been + participio. Negativa: Not having + participio. Having said that es un conector muy comun ("dicho esto / no obstante").
examples: Having finished the report, she went home.
Having been warned, he had no excuse.
Not having eaten all day, I was starving.
Having said that, the plan has risks.

sections.heading: 8 - Transformar y elegir
sections.body:
Causativo: si el trabajo lo hace otro, usa have/get + objeto + participio, conjugando have/get en el tiempo que toque.

Participios: -ing (activo: causa o simultaneidad), -ed (pasivo: pasiva reducida), Having + participio (accion anterior).

En todas, el sujeto implicito debe ser el de la oracion principal.
examples: A mechanic is servicing my car. → I'm having my car serviced.
Because she didn't know the way... → Not knowing the way...
After she had read the letter... → Having read the letter...

contrast.title: Causativo y clausulas de participio
rows: otro hace el trabajo por ti
I need to get my hair cut.

mistakes: NO: I had cut my hair at the salon. -> SI: I had my hair cut at the salon.
NO: We are painting the house by a decorator. -> SI: We are having the house painted.
NO: I got him help me. -> SI: I got him to help me. / I had him help me.
NO: Feeling tired, the meeting seemed long. -> SI: Feeling tired, I found the meeting long.
NO: Building in 1900, the house is old. -> SI: Built in 1900, the house is old.
NO: Having ate, we left. -> SI: Having eaten, we left.
NO: I need this document sign. -> SI: I need this document signed.
